deep.reconstruction:
This is a page of loose aphoristic notes from Hilbert's notebook (Cod. Ms. Hilbert 600:3, roughly 1900-1905). It contains no computations, only four separate remarks divided by horizontal rules.

(1) Statistical physics. Hilbert says it does no harm, in the molecular (kinetic) foundation of physics, to start from an improbable initial state. One should imagine having waited an infinite time and having found a suitable place in space. He adds the analogy: 'That I was born is infinitely improbable.' This is the Boltzmann-style answer to the reversibility and recurrence objections (Loschmidt, Zermelo). On that answer, a low-entropy state is a rare fluctuation in an infinitely large or long-lasting universe, and we observe it because we happen to be where it occurs.

(2) Against the theologians, i.e. against etymological or philological arguments. Knowing the root and derivation of a word gives no advantage. The conceptual meaning of words drifts completely away from their origin, so knowing the origin can even hinder understanding. Only the logical definition matters. His example is the sentence 'the real numbers are almost all irrational', which sounds paradoxical in ordinary language. The fixing of the meanings of 'rational', 'real', 'wirklich' (actual) is entirely arbitrary. In modern terms, the rationals Q are countable and have Lebesgue measure 0, so almost every real number is irrational.

(3) Completeness axiom and categoricity. Hilbert asks: to what extent does my Vollständigkeitsaxiom (completeness axiom; Grundlagen 2nd ed. 1903 and 'Über den Zahlbegriff' 1900) guarantee that the concepts (the system of all numbers, geometry, etc.) are uniquely determined? He then defines the notion. A concept is uniquely determined by axioms A if every other system of things M' satisfying A can be put in bijective correspondence with the first system M so that all properties and relations are preserved.
- In modern terms: A is categorical if any two models M and M' of A are isomorphic, via a bijection f: M -> M' with R(x1,...,xn) <-> R'(f x1,...,f xn) for every primitive relation R.
He sets as a task: prove that the system of all integers, all real numbers, Cartesian geometry etc. are such uniquely defined concepts.
- Implicit (mine): for the reals, Archimedean + completeness forces any model to be isomorphic to R, as a complete ordered field.
- Implicit (mine): for Cartesian geometry, any model of the Grundlagen axioms with completeness is isomorphic to the coordinate geometry over R.
- Implicit (mine): for the integers, Dedekind's 1888 categoricity theorem (§132).

(4) Kronecker. Kronecker's endeavour to derive certain theorems of the theory of equations directly from the coefficients, without using the existence of roots, is also an axiomatic requirement. Hilbert calls it a 'non-Archimedean' theory of equations. This ties to the previous page, where 'non-Archimedean' reasoning means proofs using a fixed number of inferences independent of the data ('gleichmässiges Schliessen', uniform reasoning). Here it means: avoid limit or continuity arguments (existence of roots via completeness) and work purely algebraically in the coefficient field. Example (mine): symmetric functions of the roots, such as the discriminant, expressed as polynomials in the coefficients.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page has no derivations.

Hilbert assumes his completeness axiom yields categoricity. This holds only in the second-order sense; first-order versions cannot be categorical (Löwenheim-Skolem), which was not an issue in his day.
His isomorphism criterion is stated informally. 'All properties and relations preserved' should be restricted to the primitive relations, as in my modern restatement.

results.what: Improbable initial state in kinetic theory justified by infinite waiting time and choice of location (fluctuation hypothesis)
results.modern_name: Boltzmann's fluctuation / anthropic answer to the recurrence objection
results.usually_credited_to: L. Boltzmann (1895 Nature letter; 1896-97 replies to Zermelo)

results.what: Definition: axioms uniquely determine a concept if any two systems satisfying them are isomorphic (structure-preserving bijection)
Programme to prove categoricity of integers, reals and Cartesian geometry via the completeness axiom
results.modern_name: Categoricity of complete ordered field / Euclidean geometry (second-order)

results.what: Kronecker's root-free algebra interpreted as a 'non-Archimedean' axiomatic demand
results.modern_name: Constructive/algebraic theory of equations (Kronecker's general arithmetic), avoidance of the fundamental theorem of algebra

results.what: Almost all real numbers are irrational
results.modern_name: Q has Lebesgue measure zero / is countable (Cantor)

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit isomorphism-based definition of 'uniquely determined by axioms' (categoricity) in Hilbert's hand around 1900-1903. It is close to Huntington and Veblen, and the link between the completeness axiom and categoricity is known from his published remarks, so this is a notable but not major unpublished detail. The rest is philosophical aphorism.

checkable.asserts: Example of an irrational real number
The rationals form a proper subset of the reals
A symmetric function of the roots (the discriminant) is computed directly from the coefficients without root existence, as in Kronecker's programme
Vieta: elementary symmetric functions of the roots equal the coefficients up to sign

'(des System aller Zahlen' is likely '(des Systems aller Zahlen' or 'der Systeme'.
'alle reelle Zahl' is likely 'aller reellen Zahlen' (abbreviated in the manuscript).
In 'die [-sell-] "reellen Zahlen' the struck word looks like 'selb', a false start; the meaning is unaffected.
